subject: Class 387 Electrostar: GW, GN, GX, HX, SN (= GX red), CC (c2c, 2016-2022)
method: Same Electrostar shell as the 377 (published 20.39 m x 2.80 m x 3.77 m vs 20.4 / 2.80 / 3.78): the 377's measured nose, car lengths, bogies and door/window positions behind the first door are kept as hypotheses and tested on photos; the Unisouth-style 387 diagrams are pixel copies of the 377 drawing so their geometry is not evidence (livery only). Bodyside x from 1D projective fits along the window band of pldn (At London 2025 838) and p174; heights up one vertical on pldn; face measured on p164 (387164 Didcot, near head-on) with per-side linear scales. m positive = right as seen head-on = the train's LEFT bodyside looking forward from the cab.

calibration.fit: u = (a x + b)/(c x + 1), a 393.84, b 1323.55, c 0.06433 (door1 front/seam/rear, windows 3-6 edges, door2 front; 12 points, rms 4.2 px, max 7.5 px)
calibration.face: p164: per-side scale from the panel's outer edge at 1.336 m (377): left 323 px/m, right 347 px/m about u0 = 640; y from the orange line's bottom edge (v 288-289) = 3.26 m; a 3-parameter projective fit over symmetric pairs (lamps, glass, frame, panel) gives the same m within 0.03 (residual <= 7 px)
calibration.notes: No rail visible on p164 or pldn: heights are anchored on the 377's orange line (3.27-3.29) and door span (0.955-3.256); the face's scale on p164 is anchored on the 377 panel width. Every number here is therefore a check of the 377 shell plus what differs from it.

trace.liveries.GX.shapes: Black window band and the broken white line, as paint. Band 1.73-2.90 m: pgxv (square-on, cab car left side) reads 1.78-2.85 at three pillars (461 px/m between the cantrail line top 3.27 and the white line 1.495; +-0.03), widened to hold the glass 1.76-2.87 and its ~0.03 m black frames. One band per bay between doors, from 0.12 m ahead of the bay's first glass to 0.12 m past its last (pgxv, pvic: rounded black frame ends next to the doors), on both cars. White line 1.47-1.52 (lineY as measured before): on the cab car it stops at 7.73 and restarts at 13.80 round the GX and its text (pgxv); on the next car the gap is the union of both sides' (left: G 7.39 to text end 13.17, right: text 6.74 to X 12.98, each with the cab car's margins 0.08 before / 0.21 after), since paint is the same both sides: 6.53-13.38. The cab car's right side (small GX, p227) keeps the left side's gap: an approximation on the far side.
trace.liveries.SN.shapes: As liveries.GX.shapes (SN is the GX red copy: see liveries.SN.copyOf).
trace.liveries.GX.shapes.lineFront: The cab car's white line starts at the cab door's front edge 0.985 (cab.doors[0] 1.435 - 0.45), not ahead of it at -1: s-cab-205 (both readers: 'white line starting at the cab door', 'cream line from the door rearwards') and pvic (387227, left side: the line begins at the cab door seal; the cab corner with the mirror pod and rounded window is plain red). It runs across the cab door. The 387-GX elevation (16 samples, 2026-10-05) had it from the nose at 0.125. SN (copyOf GX) changed with it
trace.face.gangwayFrame.bellows: Bellows (the gangway's sides between face and frame): grey rubber, darker and warmer than the pipeline's default #9A9EA2. Sampled on 379 g018 (crop f-gangway-018, the lit side of the folds, x 20-110 y 200-800: median #5E5A51) and balanced against the white bodyside in the same light (white-018 #A7A69F -> #F0F0F0): #87827A. The same Bombardier gangway on every gangwayed Electrostar; readers of this class's gangway crops see the same grey pleated bellows, so the 379 value is used.
trace.liveries.GX.body: Signal red, as the face: red-coo #CC1608 (overcast daylight, raw, iqr 2-3). The station-lit pvic balanced on the thin white line gave #C22651, which renders crimson-pink beside every daylight photo (387-GX sheet, 2026-10-06); red-205 in shade (#8B1E1C) has the same hue as red-coo, not vic's. The face takes the same red (it read #C22651 too, against this trace's own note that the face uses red-coo).
trace.liveries.GW.body: GWR green as the 800 has it (#0B3D2E, liveries/GW.ts and classes/800/spec.json): the raw p174 samples (#314B5A, #2C434F) carry the overcast sky's blue with no white on the car to balance against, and rendered blue-teal beside every photo, which all read near-black green (pairs reader, 2026-10-06). Face the same; the band 1.5x the body as the diagram gives it.
trace.liveries.SN.choice: The livery rule (2026-10-06, FLEET.md): each class x operator renders the livery most units carry today; on a near tie, the newer scheme. The 387/2s Southern works (with Gatwick Express) carry the red Gatwick Express scheme with its GX marks (387207, 387220, 387223, 387227: 2025-26 photos); no 387 in Southern livery or with a Southern logo is on Commons. liveries.SN is that red scheme with its marks.
